report:
PASS for the restricted A–F and their supplied proof dependency chain. No essential mathematical gap remains in this scope. The unrestricted original P03 remains unresolved by these materials: no argument establishes the constant-minimum antecedent for arbitrary strictly LCK metrics, and neither Hopf family is a counterexample.

I compared the entire article, the full historical review, and all eight ordinary notes. The support DAG is valid and acyclic: n1 is independent; n2 uses n1; n3 uses n1,n2; n4 uses n1,n2,n3; n5 uses n1,n3; n6 uses n2,n5; n7 uses n1,n3,n5; n8 summarizes n1–n7. Each mathematical support was checked directly. The historical INCONCLUSIVE verdict and candidate=false correctly concern unrestricted P03; neither was used as proof authority. Referenced private paths and execution artifacts were not opened.

A: The radial primitive construction in n1 differentiates to λ on a coordinate ball. Thus λ=df locally, λᶜ=dᶜf and κ=−ddᶜf, with exactly ddᶜ=i∂bar∂/(2π). This establishes reality, type (1,1), and closedness. The global primitive −λᶜ establishes de Rham exactness. Direct differentiation gives the conformal transformations λ′=λ+da and κ′=κ−ddᶜa, preserving both relevant classes. Ordinary Bott–Chern nontriviality is established separately by n3: if κ=ddᶜa globally, the actual metric e^aω has zero curvature and still has nonexact Lee form. Applying B’s first identity to that metric produces a strictly positive integral with zero left side. Taking real parts supplies a real potential if Bott–Chern exactness was initially expressed using a complex function. This proof does not identify de Rham and Bott–Chern triviality.

B: Writing α=λ¹⁰ gives Q=iα∧conjugate(α)/(2π), a semipositive rank-one form wherever λ≠0. Nonexactness ensures a nonempty open set of such points. The graded Leibniz rule, including the degree-one sign, gives
 d(λᶜ∧κ^(k−1)∧ω^(n−k))=−κ^k∧ω^(n−k)+(n−k)Q∧κ^(k−1)∧ω^(n−k).
Compact Stokes proves all identities for 1≤k≤n. The cases k=1 and k=n give the strictly positive first integral and zero top integral; n≥2 is essential for strict positivity.

For η_t=ω+tκ, the crucial identity is dη_t=λ∧ω. Consequently Stokes gives ∫κ∧η_t^(n−1)=(n−1)∫Q∧ω∧η_t^(n−2), and differentiation gives the claimed V′(t). When η_t is positive, the mixed wedge is nonnegative everywhere and strictly positive wherever Q≠0. In an η_t-unitary coframe placing Q in one direction, this reduces to the positive trace of ω on the complementary directions. This includes n=2. The coefficient of t^n is ∫κ^n=0. Neither calculation requires a Gauduchon condition.

C: Under the explicit antecedent that the least relative eigenvalue r is constant, r<0 would make η_t positive for 0≤t<T=−1/r. At T it is semipositive with a kernel at every point, hence V(T)=0. Strict increase and polynomial continuity instead give V(T)≥V(0)>0. Thus κ is semipositive. Its continuous nonnegative top power has zero integral, so it vanishes everywhere, forcing the least eigenvalue to be zero everywhere. This uses neither constancy of the remaining eigenvalues nor constancy of rank. The smooth closed semipositive κ itself proves pseudoeffectivity, and A proves that its class is nonzero.

The every-test consequence is direct, without Lamari sufficiency. The two integrations by parts in n1 have the correct signs and give ∫ddᶜu∧γ^(n−1)=∫u ddᶜ(γ^(n−1))=0 for every positive Gauduchon γ. A smooth semipositive representative therefore yields nonnegative pairing against every such test. In these constructions the representative is nonzero, so those pairings are actually strictly positive. The smooth corrections are genuinely quasi-plurisubharmonic, as their Levi forms are locally bounded below.

If the entire spectrum is constant, rank is constant, nonzero by B, and at most n−1. On an actual compact quotient, the lifted invariant tensors and their type derivatives have constant coefficients in an invariant frame, establishing the required constant spectrum. This does not require a group action on the quotient preserving these tensors. For any invariant Hermitian γ, ddᶜγ^(n−1)=bγ^n for a real constant b; Stokes and ∫γ^n>0 force b=0. Thus every such invariant metric is Gauduchon. No lattice existence or classification premise enters.

D: Scalar contraction acts freely and properly discontinuously, since compact subsets of the punctured space have radii bounded above and away from zero. Polar coordinates identify the quotient smoothly with S^(2n−1)×(R/(log 2)Z); local holomorphic quotient charts establish the compact connected complex manifold. The bounds (1−ε)ρ≤Φ≤(1+ε)ρ prove positivity for every permitted ε. Both Φ and Ω scale by 1/4, so ω and λ descend. Closedness of Ω proves the LCK equation. The loop lifted from z to z/2 has Lee period 2 log 2, proving nonexactness.

The logarithmic Hessian is I/Φ−FF*/Φ², with F_i=conjugate(z_i)+εz_1δ_i1. Relative to ω it has spectrum consisting of n−1 ones and 1−|F|²/Φ. At e1 this gives −ε,1,…,1. The correction u=logρ−logΦ is smooth, deck-invariant and bounded between −log(1+ε) and −log(1−ε). Its corrected curvature is ddᶜlogρ, whose Levi form is nonnegative by Cauchy–Schwarz, with kernel Cz and rank n−1. Hence the negative eigenvalue of the original representative does not disprove pseudoeffectivity.

E: Substitution of z1=x+iy gives exactly the stated h. The identities (h+ε)Φ=ε[2(1−ε)y²+R] and (ε−h)Φ=ε[2(1+ε)x²+R] prove both bounds, attained at e1 and ie1. Since ε<1, h is the least eigenvalue. The ray factors are 1+t, repeated n−1 times, and 1+th; therefore the first positive boundary is precisely 1/ε. Its exceptional factor vanishes exactly when y=0 and R=0. The boundary top power is nonnegative everywhere and positive on an open set, so its integral remains positive. This correctly distinguishes partial degeneration from C’s everywhere degeneration.

I also checked n6’s supplementary statements. The determinant identities κ^n=hω^n and η_t^n=(1+t)^(n−1)(1+th)ω^n, together with B, give ∫hω^n=0 and V(t)=(1+t)^(n−1)V(0) for all real t as a polynomial identity. The full positivity interval is −1<t<1/ε. These are correct supplementary results; this verdict does not extend the article’s stated A–F release.

F: With a=q/s, the complex chain rule gives the all-dimensional identity
 H_(q²/s)(v)=(2/s)|conjugate(z1)v1−aΣconjugate(zj)vj|²+2a|v1|²−a²|v|².
The first two terms are nonnegative and 0≤a≤1, proving Ω_ε≥(1−ε)ddᶜs>0 for every stipulated ε. Homogeneity proves descent of Ω_ε/s; differentiation proves its LCK equation, and the same loop proves the Lee period. Curvature is ddᶜlog s, semipositive of rank n−1, so its least relative eigenvalue is identically zero. At e1 the Hessian of q²/s is diag(1,−1,…,−1), giving the asserted n−1 eigenvalues 1/(1−ε). At e2 its Hessian vanishes, giving n−1 ones. These points exist and are distinct in every n≥2, and the spectra differ for every allowed ε>0. Thus least-only constancy is strictly weaker than entire-spectrum constancy. This family also has a smooth positive-current representative and is no counterexample.

No indispensable nonroutine external theorem is needed. I opened the [Ornea–Verbitsky primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595v2), confirming the cited historical Conjecture 5.13, and [Lamari’s primary paper](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.1673.pdf), checking the contextual Lemma 3.3 and its separate zero-pairing case. Neither theorem supplies a proof step here. Classification, Gauduchon existence, duality sufficiency, current regularization and symbolic execution are unnecessary. Accordingly premises and passages are empty.

Harmless wording clarifications: ∫η_t^n is n! times the usual Hermitian metric volume, consistently with the stipulated ordinary powers. The potentials and automorphic forms Ω,Ω_ε live on the cover; the LCK forms, Lee forms, curvature and stated correction descend, as the article’s scaling calculations explicitly show. No substantial repair is required. Remaining mathematical gaps concern only unrestricted P03, outside this scoped PASS; no worldwide current-status or priority claim is certified.
